item.title: Tupelo man sentenced to 12 years to serve for fentanyl trafficking - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A Tupelo man has been sentenced to 12 years in prison after pleading guilty to trafficking fentanyl, according to the First Circuit District Attorney’s Office.

The district attorney’s office said Alderius Rashad Morrow entered the guilty plea Monday before Circuit Court Judge Kelly L. Mims.

Mims sentenced Morrow to 40 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections, with 28 years suspended, leaving 12 years to serve, according to the release.

Because the conviction was for a trafficking offense, Morrow is not eligible for parole or early release and must serve the full 12-year sentence day for day, the district attorney’s office said.

The case was investigated by the North Mississippi Narcotics Unit.

Assistant District Attorney Megan French prosecuted the case for the state, according to the release.

item.title: Survey: Mississippi sports fans name two top picks for scattering their ashes - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Some of y’all really are sports fans to the death. Like literally, to the death.

A new national survey examining the emotional ties between sports fans and their favorite teams found that Mississippi fans would most want their ashes scattered at two of the state’s most iconic college football stadiums.

Not surprisingly, it’s Davis Wade Stadium and Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.

The poll, conducted by SportsbookReview.com , surveyed 3,013 sports fans across the country and asked participants which sports venue they would choose as a final resting place if given the option.

Mississippi State University’s Davis Wade Stadium in Starkville ranked first among Mississippi fans. The stadium, home to Bulldogs football since 1914, is known nationally for its cowbell tradition and game-day atmosphere on Scott Field.

Survey organizers said many fans view the stadium as more than a sports venue, describing it as a place tied to decades of memories, traditions and identity.

Second on the Mississippi list was Ole Miss’ Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford. Opened in 1915 and located adjacent to the Grove, the stadium is associated with the university’s well-known tailgating culture and longstanding football traditions.

The survey found that emotional attachment played a major role in fans’ choices. About 26% of respondents cited memories involving family, friends and childhood experiences as the primary reason for their connection to a stadium, while 25% pointed to lifelong support for a team.

Another 17% described stadiums as feeling like a “second home,” while 13% said the venues represented part of their identity.

Researchers also found that many fans would prefer their ashes scattered directly on the playing surface, with 64% selecting the field or court over seating areas or spaces outside the stadium.

Nationally, some of the most commonly selected venues included Wrigley Field, Fenway Park, Madison Square Garden, Lambeau Field and Dodger Stadium.

The survey also explored whether fans believed ash scattering should be permitted in sports venues. A slight majority, 54%, said they supported allowing it in controlled circumstances.

James Bisson, editor-in-chief of SportsbookReview.com, said the findings reflect how sports venues often become deeply tied to personal history and community identity.

“What we’re seeing here isn’t just about fandom — it’s about memory, identity and belonging,” Bisson said.

item.title: Ridgeland Students Launch ‘WORTH A LISTEN’ Mental Health Initiative - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RIDGELAND — Students with the Ridgeland Mayor’s Youth Council are launching a new mental health awareness initiative aimed at reducing stigma, increasing access to resources and encouraging conversations among young people across the metro area.

The initiative, called “WORTH A LISTEN,” is a collaboration between the youth council, Killebrew Psychological Services and Essential Touchstones.

Organizers said the student-led effort will initially roll out in six metro-area schools attended by members of the Ridgeland Mayor’s Youth Council, with plans to eventually expand statewide. The program will include student-led awareness campaigns, mental health resource distribution, school and community outreach efforts, and partnerships with local and state mental health organizations.

Ridgeland Mayor Gene McGee said the initiative reflects growing concerns about the mental health challenges facing students.

“Young people today are facing pressures and challenges unlike any generation before them,” McGee said. “‘WORTH A LISTEN’ sends a powerful message that their voices matter, their struggles are seen, and help is always available.”

According to organizers, the idea for the initiative emerged after students applying to the Mayor’s Youth Council were asked to identify the biggest issues affecting their peers. Officials said 95% of applicants cited mental health concerns, including anxiety, depression, bullying and social media addiction.

Lisa Walters, the mayor’s chief of staff and coordinator of the youth council, said the responses made it clear the issue could not be ignored. Mental health professionals with Killebrew Psychological Services and Essential Touchstones later joined the effort to help shape the program and provide clinical guidance.

Dr. Alyssa Killebrew said the initiative is especially meaningful because it is being driven by students themselves.

“What makes this initiative so powerful is that it is coming directly from students who recognize the need among their own peers,” Killebrew said.

National research cited by organizers shows youth mental health concerns continue to rise. Studies from organizations including the National Alliance on Mental Illness and the American Psychological Association indicate that nearly 40% of high school students report persistent feelings of sadness or hopelessness, while roughly two in five young people experience a diagnosable mental health condition each year.

Student leaders involved in the initiative said they hope the program encourages peers to seek help and support one another.

“So many students feel like they have to handle everything on their own,” said Ashwin Talwar, a member of the youth council. “This initiative is about making sure everyone knows there is someone who will listen and that it’s okay to ask for help.”

City leaders said they hope “WORTH A LISTEN” becomes a long-term movement focused on improving mental health awareness and support systems for students throughout Mississippi.

item.title: Pearl River County search warrant turns up suspected marijuana, THC vapes and cash - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PICAYUNE – Two people were arrested after a narcotics search warrant was executed at a residence in Picayune, according to the Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department.

The sheriff’s department said its Narcotics Division, with help from the Patrol Division, served the warrant April 29 at a home on Cabin Drive.

During the search, investigators seized what authorities described as a large quantity of suspected marijuana, THC vape products, digital scales, packaging materials and U.S. currency believed to be tied to illegal drug distribution.

The sheriff’s department identified the two occupants as Catherine Zirkle, 24, and Dylan Revolta, 24, both of the Cabin Drive address in Picayune.

Both were taken to the Pearl River County Criminal Justice Facility and charged with trafficking a controlled substance and possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance, according to the sheriff’s department.

Sheriff David Allison thanked deputies and investigators for their work in combating illegal drug activity in Pearl River County.

Anyone with information about narcotics activity is asked to contact the Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department at 601-403-2582.

item.title: Mississippi opens statewide applications for private land alligator tags for 2026 season - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Mississippi landowners across the state can now apply for private land alligator tags for the 2026 season, according to the state’s private lands and permits information.

Officials said the private lands alligator tag program is available statewide beginning in 2026.

Applications for private lands alligator permits will be accepted from May 1 through July 1, and all applications must be submitted online, according to the state.

There is no fee to apply.

Officials said anyone may submit an application for a property in open counties as long as the landowner signs the application. Only one application may be submitted for each property.

The 2026 alligator season opens on the last Friday in August, which falls on Aug. 28 this year.

According to the state, the private lands season will run from noon Aug. 28 until 6 a.m. Sept. 21.

item.title: Mississippi Attorney General finds use of force justified in four line of duty shootings - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Attorney General’s Office announced Monday it has completed reviews of four line of duty shootings across the state and determined the use of force was justified in each case.

According to the Attorney General’s Office, the reviews were conducted following investigations by the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation, as required under Mississippi law.

One of the incidents reviewed occurred July 9, 2022, in Jackson and involved an officer with the Jackson Police Department near the former Canton Apartments on Southwest Street. This was during a period of time when Jackson Police Department was not releasing all information to the media or the public and we’re working to confirm what happened.

Another case stemmed from a Feb. 21, 2024, pursuit in Lake Cormorant involving deputies with the DeSoto County Sheriff’s Office. Investigators said deputies executed a PIT maneuver after a vehicle pursuit near U.S. 61 south of Mississippi 3. Authorities said the suspect, identified as 35-year-old Jamarcus Brown, fired at a K-9 after deputies released the dog. Deputies returned fire, killing Brown. The K-9, Luca, suffered serious injuries and later died shortly before retirement.

The Attorney General’s Office also reviewed an Oct. 15, 2024, shooting in Jackson involving a Jackson police officer. Police said the incident began on Interstate 220 after a collision involving a stolen Volvo. Authorities alleged 47-year-old Anthony Johnson fired shots at an 18-wheeler driver before later pointing a weapon at narcotics detectives, who then shot him in the lower extremities. Johnson was charged with two counts of aggravated assault on a law enforcement officer and possession of a stolen vehicle.

The fourth incident occurred Dec. 31, 2024, in Ridgeland and involved a detective with the Ridgeland Police Department. Investigators said detectives located a stolen vehicle at Renaissance at Colony Park near Barnes & Noble. Authorities said a 15-year-old suspect struck a detective with the vehicle as officers approached. The detective fired his weapon, striking the suspect, who then fled before crashing near Watkins Drive and Interstate 220. The teen was later arrested and charged with multiple offenses, including aggravated assault on a police officer and receiving stolen property.

The Attorney General’s Office said all four reviews concluded the officers’ actions were legally justified under Mississippi law.

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: Elester Womack, Covington County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
COLLINS — Nearly four years after he disappeared, the whereabouts of Elester Womack remain unknown, and the lack of information about it leaves investigators searching for answers.

Womack, also known to family and friends as “Farrell,” was last seen on or around June 3, 2022, in Covington County, according to the Covington County Sheriff’s Department.

Very few details have been released publicly about the circumstances surrounding his disappearance.

At the time he vanished, Womack was 61 years old. He is a Black male with black hair and brown eyes, standing 5 feet 7 inches tall and weighing about 178 pounds.

Authorities and family members have continued to ask the public for information in hopes of generating new leads in the case.

Older adults represent a smaller share of missing persons cases nationwide, but advocates say those disappearances can present unique challenges. FBI missing person data shows hundreds of thousands of people are reported missing in the United States each year, including tens of thousands of adults. Cases involving seniors can involve anything from medical conditions to confusion to foul play or unexplained circumstances like Womack.

Metro Crime Stoppers joined the search effort, offering anonymous tip options and possible cash rewards for information leading to progress in the investigation.

Anyone with information about Womack’s disappearance is urged to contact the Covington County Sheriff’s Department at 601-765-8281 or Metro Crime Stoppers at 601-582-STOP. Tips may also be submitted online through P3Tips.com .

item.title: Louisiana man killed in crash on Interstate 10 in Harrison County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
HARRISON COUNTY — A 43-year-old Louisiana man was killed Friday evening in a single-vehicle crash on Interstate 10 in Harrison County, according to the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

Troopers responded to the crash around 5:20 p.m. on May 1.

Authorities said Wilmer Rodriguez of Kenner, Louisiana, was driving a 2007 Honda Accord westbound on I-10 when the vehicle ran off the roadway, overturned and struck a tree.

Rodriguez sustained fatal injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene, officials said. The crash remains under investigation by the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

item.title: JSU twins honor late father, earn master’s in speech-language pathology - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
By William H. Kelly III Jackson State University

JACKSON — Twin sisters Ebonee and Ebonea’ Harrison, 28, earned their master’s degrees in speech-language pathology and audiology from Jackson State University, accomplishing yet another major milestone together.

The St. James Parish, Louisiana, natives graduated on Friday, May 1, celebrating sisterhood and stepping into a career they chose in honor of their late father.

Prior to their birth, their father endured a tragic collision with a train that left him in a week-long coma, paralyzed on one side of his body, and unable to speak due to a traumatic brain injury. Sadly, as they approached their 16th birthday, the girls and their father were caught in a devastating car accident with a drunk driver that ultimately took his life.

Growing up, the twins’ mom would play home videos and share stories about their dad’s recovery and how physical therapy and a speech pathologist were instrumental in restoring his mobility and voice back to “normal.”

“For him to be able to communicate and still be able to express himself, and take care of us, was a big thing. It was an eye-opener for us, and we wanted to come into this field based on that,” they shared. “We wanted to come into this career and change lives as well.”

Speech-language pathologists utilize tools such as Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) devices, Picture Exchange Communication System® (PECS®), and non-verbal gestures to assist people with communicating.

“Everyone’s voice deserves to be heard no matter what, and everyone deserves a chance to communicate,” Ebonea’ shared.

While navigating the graduate program at JSU the siblings’ passion for speech-language pathology grew deeper through hands-on clinical training at facilities like Brookdale Senior Living in Clinton, Methodist Rehabilitation and Smart Therapy, LLC, Pediatric Rehabiliation Clinic.

The twins learned to service children and adult clients who ranged from being non-verbal, blind, hearing impaired, and autistic, or suffered from dementia, strokes, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and more.

Both Ebonee and Ebonea’ believe that interacting directly with patients reminded them of the role they hope to serve in communities throughout Mississippi and Louisiana.

“Being in our clinical placements showed us how hard it is for some people to communicate, and the big role we play in their lives to help them communicate,” said Ebonee. “Communication is essential for life, and everyone should be able to communicate in some aspect.”

Ebonee and Ebonea’ look forward to what’s next. They currently have over three job offers at the same skilled nursing facility, pediatric clinic, and elementary school.

“I love this field, and being here really made me love it even more. It didn’t sway me away,” said Ebonea’. “I learned a ton at Jackson State University that I don’t think I would have learned anywhere else.”

item.title: Hurricane Awareness week offers Mississippi a familiar reminder: Be prepared - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Gulf Coast has faced the order to evacuate at least seven times since Hurricane Katrina reshaped the coastline in 2005. For residents of the southern counties, the drill is practically institutional: pack up, load the car, head north on I-55, I-59, or MS-49 and hope for the best.

But hope is not a preparedness plan.

Governor Tate Reeves has declared May 3-9 as Hurricane Preparedness Week, and both the Mississippi Emergency Management Agency and the Mississippi Insurance Department are using the occasion to push residents toward concrete action before the Atlantic hurricane season officially begins June 1.

“Over the last several years, our state has confronted many natural disasters including hurricanes, tornadoes, floods, and ice storms,” Reeves said. “It is critical to have a plan before severe weather strikes. It can make a difference in keeping you and your family safe. I hope Hurricane Preparedness Week can help raise awareness about the upcoming hurricane season and encourage Mississippians to take the necessary steps to prepare.”

Last year’s Atlantic season produced 13 named storms, five of which became hurricanes and four of which intensified into major hurricanes, just above the historical average of three major hurricanes per season, according to the National Weather Service.

That proximity to average can be deceiving. The Gulf Coast has learned repeatedly that it does not take a record-breaking season to produce catastrophic results. Gustav and Ike hit in back-to-back weeks in September 2008, forcing two rounds of coastal mobilization within the same season.

Hurricane Isaac in 2012, a slow-moving Category 1 that might have seemed manageable on paper, triggered mandatory evacuations in all three coastal counties, dropped 17 inches of rain on Kiln, and ultimately housed more than 2,100 evacuees in shelters statewide.

Hurricane Zeta in 2020 caused an estimated $1.25 billion in damage to the coast, knocked out power to roughly half a million customers, and put more than 3,000 people in shelters. Hurricane Ida prompted mandatory evacuations across low-lying areas of Hancock County just a year later.

The pattern stretches back two decades and beyond, to the storm that still defines the conversation: Hurricane Katrina. Waveland, nearly wiped off the map by Katrina’s storm surge in 2005, did not get its police department back into a permanent building until 2016 , eleven years after the storm. The lesson the coast learned at enormous cost is the same one state officials are repeating this week: the time to prepare is before the season starts, not after the forecast cone appears on the evening news.

“I encourage all Mississippians to use Hurricane Preparedness Week to prepare now, by assembling an emergency supply kit, developing a family emergency plan, and determining evacuation routes,” said MEMA Executive Director Stephen McCraney. “By taking precautions now, we can safeguard our communities from any potential tropical storms. Let’s work together to ensure the safety and resilience of Mississippi during this hurricane season.”

MEMA will highlight a specific preparedness topic each day of the week on its social media platforms, moving from “Know Your Risk” on Sunday through “Take Action Today” on Saturday. item.title: Beloved Malayan tiger Bunga undergoing treatment at Hattiesburg Zoo - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HATTIESBURG – The Hattiesburg Zoo says Bunga, its Malayan tiger, is undergoing medical treatment for several health concerns, including high blood pressure and significant disc disease.

According to the zoo, Bunga had two nosebleed episodes about two weeks ago and was later diagnosed with hypertension. Hattiesburg Zoo veterinarian Dr. Julia MacGregor started him on medication to manage the condition.

The zoo said Bunga initially showed some improvement, but staff noticed changes in his behavior late last week, including increased lethargy and signs of discomfort.

Zoo officials said Bunga was taken Wednesday to Animal Medical Center in Hattiesburg, where he underwent a CT scan to look for possible underlying causes of his symptoms.

The scan showed significant disc disease, especially in his neck, which the zoo said is likely causing discomfort and some mobility changes. Bunga’s bloodwork was largely normal, according to the zoo.

“Bunga’s case is complex, and our team is working diligently to manage multiple conditions at once,” MacGregor said in a statement. “Our immediate priority is to keep him comfortable while stabilizing his blood pressure.”

The zoo said its veterinary team has adjusted Bunga’s medications by increasing treatment for his blood pressure and adding pain management for chronic and nerve-related discomfort.

Zoo officials said Bunga has shown sensitivity to certain medications in the past, so staff are carefully balancing treatment to make sure it is both safe and effective.

Bunga is also continuing treatment for inflammatory bowel disease, a condition the zoo said he was diagnosed with last year.

The zoo said animal care staff are monitoring him closely and that all decisions are being made with his quality of life as the top priority.

“Our focus is always on Bunga’s wellbeing,” zoo officials said. “We are committed to providing the highest level of care and making thoughtful, compassionate decisions every step of the way.”

MacGregor also praised the zoo’s veterinary and animal care teams for training Bunga to voluntarily participate in parts of his care, including blood draws and blood pressure checks. The zoo said that training allows for more frequent monitoring without the need for full immobilization.

Bunga has been a longtime favorite among visitors and serves as an ambassador for Malayan tigers, which are critically endangered, according to the zoo.

The Hattiesburg Zoo said it will continue to monitor Bunga and share updates when appropriate.

item.title: Attorney General Lynn Fitch joins 41 attorneys general urging feds to leave sports betting oversight to states - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch has joined a bipartisan coalition of 41 attorneys general urging federal regulators to reaffirm that states, not the federal government, should oversee sports-related event contracts tied to betting.

According to Fitch’s office, the coalition filed a formal comment with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission arguing that so-called prediction markets have effectively become unregulated sportsbooks.

“Mississippi, like many states, has carefully balanced competing interests to allow responsible sports betting here,” Fitch said in a statement. “The CFTC should not upend that balance, usurp state authorities without a clear Congressional directive, and leave states with the responsibility for cleaning up the impacts of sports betting without the ability to regulate it on the front end.”

The coalition said prediction market platforms allow users to wager on outcomes such as game winners, point spreads and player statistics while bypassing state gambling regulations and consumer protections.

In the comment letter, the attorneys general argued that there is no meaningful difference for consumers between traditional sports bets and sports-related event contracts offered on designated contract markets.

The coalition contends that those contracts do not serve the traditional purposes of derivatives markets, such as hedging or price discovery, and instead function as entertainment-based gambling, which they say falls under state authority.

The attorneys general also warned that sports gambling can pose risks to public health and financial security and said states are better equipped than the CFTC to regulate or prohibit such activity.

The letter was filed in response to a CFTC request for public comment on proposed rules for prediction markets. The coalition urged the agency to confirm through rulemaking that it does not have jurisdiction over sports-related contracts.

Fitch joined attorneys general from 40 other states and the District of Columbia in signing the letter.

item.title: Man arrested after traffic stop leads to foot chase through Laurel business - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LAUREL – An Ellisville man was arrested Saturday after a traffic stop in Laurel turned into a foot chase that ended inside a local business, according to the Jones County Sheriff’s Department.

Authorities said Deputy Clay Sullivan stopped a Toyota Tundra on First Street in front of Sol Plaza after seeing the driver allegedly driving recklessly on Interstate 59 and later on 16th Avenue in Laurel.

The driver, identified as 36-year-old Antonio Calihua of Ellisville, got out of the truck and aggressively resisted being detained before running away on foot, according to the sheriff’s department.

During the chase, Sullivan deployed his Taser, authorities said. Calihua then ran through the front door of Sol Plaza and into the store, causing damage to merchandise and fixtures, according to investigators.

Sullivan called for backup and tackled Calihua inside the business, the sheriff’s department said. Authorities said Calihua continued resisting arrest until additional units from the Jones County Sheriff’s Department and Laurel Police Department arrived.

Calihua was taken into custody and transported to South Central Regional Medical Center in Laurel for treatment of a cut he suffered while resisting arrest, according to authorities.

He is charged with first-offense DUI, resisting arrest, disorderly conduct, no insurance, no driver’s license and reckless driving.

The sheriff’s department said Calihua is being held in the Jones County Adult Detention Facility pending his initial appearance in Jones County Justice Court.

item.title: DNA match leads to arrest in 2025 Prentiss County burglary case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PRENTISS COUNTY – A 33-year-old Prentiss County man has been arrested in connection with a 2025 burglary after a DNA sample recovered at the scene matched him through a state database, according to the Prentiss County Sheriff’s Department.

Authorities said Daniel Stout of County Road 4101 was arrested April 30 in the case.

The investigation began Aug. 23, 2025, when Deputy Dennis Peeks responded to a residence at 369 County Road 4101 after the homeowner reported a forced entry and multiple stolen items, according to the sheriff’s department.

Investigators said evidence collected at the scene included a blood sample recovered from a broken window.

In April 2026, the Mississippi Forensics Laboratory notified investigators that the DNA sample produced a CODIS match to Stout.

The sheriff’s department said investigators then contacted Stout, who later admitted to committing the burglary.

Stout was taken into custody and transported to the Prentiss County Jail.

He has been charged with burglary of a commercial building. Justice Court Judge Ray Hall set his bond at $25,000 cash or professional bond only, the sheriff’s department said.

Investigator Aaron Stolz will present the case to the next Prentiss County grand jury. Investigator Torie Jumper also assisted in the investigation.

item.title: Cheshire Abbey asks for donations as rescue faces air conditioner repair cost and overcrowding - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Cheshire Abbey is asking for donations and community support as the rescue struggles with rising costs, overcrowding and limited staffing.

Chrissy Cheshire has dedicated her life to helping and saving the forgotten animals dumped in Jackson and now she needs the community to step up.

In a post on Facebook, the rescue said it is caring for more than 70 animals and is beyond full capacity. The organization said increasing expenses and the demands of daily care have put significant strain on operations.

According to Cheshire Abbey, its Entergy bill reached $623 this month, and a recent air conditioner repair cost $800. The rescue said it is also facing ongoing expenses for staff, internet, phone, security, water, trash and supplies.

The group said weekly bulk food costs run about $400, and monthly preventatives for the animals are expected to cost about $1,000. Cheshire Abbey also said one of its veterinary accounts has climbed back above $16,000 after recent payments.

The rescue said it is currently being run with only one full-time worker and warned it may soon be forced to stop responding to calls for help because of limited space, time and manpower.

Cheshire Abbey said it is seeking donations, corporate sponsors and additional help to continue caring for the animals already in its custody.

Donations can be made through the rescue’s online payment accounts, by mail, at participating pet supply stores or directly to veterinary clinics used by the organization.

Please consider skipping your weekly Starbucks run and donate to this rescue that does so much for the community.

item.title: Jackson fire rating drops to Class 4; water pressure cited as key factor - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The City of Jackson and the Jackson Fire Department say a recent downgrade in the city’s fire protection rating is largely tied to ongoing water system issues, including insufficient water pressure in some areas.

City officials confirmed the Public Protection Classification rating dropped from a Class 3 to a Class 4 following a routine evaluation. The rating, issued by the Mississippi State Rating Bureau, considers factors such as fire department operations, emergency response capabilities and water system performance.

Officials said reliable water pressure is critical for firefighting and that deficiencies in the system played a major role in the lower rating. The change could lead to higher property insurance premiums for some residents and business owners, as insurers often use fire ratings to assess risk.

The city emphasized that it does not operate the water system. Water service, including pressure levels, is managed by JXN Water, the federally appointed entity overseeing Jackson’s water infrastructure.

Despite the downgrade, city leaders pointed to improvements within the fire department, including increased staffing and operational upgrades. The department currently employs 255 firefighters, with about 85 assigned per shift, and has added 29 firefighters since July 2025 under Mayor John Horhn’s administration.

Officials said the department has also strengthened training, inspections, code enforcement and equipment testing in response to state evaluations.

City leaders noted the rating could have been worse. According to the Mississippi State Rating Bureau, Jackson’s classification would have dropped to a Class 5 without corrective actions taken by March 2026. The bureau also commended Fire Chief RaSean Thomas and his team for their efforts.

The city said it will continue working with JXN Water and state officials to address remaining issues and improve the rating in future reviews.

item.title: Woman dies in Rankin County house fire - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – A woman died Thursday morning after a house fire in Rankin County, according to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Office.

The sheriff’s office said deputies received a 911 call at about 7:50 a.m. reporting a structure fire at 170 Bain Road in Puckett. The caller told authorities the home was on fire and that a female victim was still inside.

Fire crews from the Puckett, Cato and Walters fire departments responded along with Rankin County deputies, Rankin County Emergency Operations Center and Pafford Ambulance, authorities said.

First responders extinguished the fire and found an unresponsive woman inside a bedroom of the residence, according to the sheriff’s office. Despite lifesaving efforts, the woman died at the scene.

Rankin County Coroner David Ruth responded and took custody of the body. Authorities said the victim’s name will be released after family members are notified.

Rankin County Sheriff’s Office fire investigators and the State Fire Marshal’s Office are investigating the cause of the fire.

Authorities said their prayers are with the victim’s family and the first responders who responded to the scene.

item.title: Starkville Police to launch weekend managed access area in Cotton District - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
STARKVILLE — The Starkville Police Department will begin operating a managed access area in the Cotton District on weekend nights for the foreseeable future in an effort to improve public safety in the popular entertainment district.

The managed access area will operate Fridays and Saturdays from 10 p.m. to 1 a.m., according to police.

Officials said the initiative is designed to address safety concerns in high-traffic areas by controlling entry into portions of the district during peak nightlife hours.

Under the new guidelines, visitors entering the area must present a valid ID, be at least 18 years old and obtain a wristband at one of four designated entry points. Police also said backpacks, outside beverages, masks and face coverings will not be permitted inside the controlled area.

An additional entry point may be opened as needed, depending on crowd size and traffic conditions.

The department also announced temporary traffic adjustments connected to the managed access area. Drivers traveling west toward University Drive from Barr Avenue and Camp Avenue will be able to use alternate routes to bypass the Cotton District. Motorists traveling north on Colonel Muldrow Drive will be redirected east toward Barr Avenue and Camp Avenue.

Police released a traffic map detailing routes, closures and entry locations associated with the new operation.

item.title: Sharkey County sheriff's office upgrades booking process with electronic fingerprint system - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
SHARKEY COUNTY — The Sharkey County Sheriff’s Department has acquired a new electronic fingerprinting system that will allow deputies to capture and transmit fingerprints and mugshots directly to the state, replacing a slower, more error-prone process.

The department recently purchased an IDEMIA LiveScan system using grant funding secured by department employee Angela Jenkins, Sheriff Herbert D. Ceaser Sr. announced.

The system electronically captures fingerprints, palm prints and facial images at the time of booking and transmits them directly to state databases, cutting down on paperwork and turnaround time. It can also flag whether a subject has previously been booked under a different identity and link individuals to records in other law enforcement databases.

Previously, fingerprinting in many smaller jurisdictions relied on ink-based methods that required manual processing and mailing to state agencies, a process that could take days and was more susceptible to errors that led to rejected submissions.

The IDEMIA system uses FBI-certified scanners and is compatible with existing records management systems. It supports multiple types of biometric data, including fingerprints, palm prints, photographs, iris scans and documentation of scars, marks and tattoos.

Sharkey County is one of the smaller sheriff’s departments in the state. Grant-funded technology acquisitions like this one have become an increasingly common way for rural law enforcement agencies to access equipment that would otherwise be out of reach for departments with limited budgets.

item.title: Pearl River County man loses final appeal in 2020 Picayune murder - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
PEARL RIVER COUNTY — A Pearl River County man convicted of killing a friend for his cash will spend the rest of his life in prison after Mississippi’s highest court refused last week to hear his case.

The Mississippi Supreme Court declined on April 22 to review Austin Brookshire’s conviction in the 2020 shooting death of Willie Jones, leaving intact a September appeals court ruling that upheld his life sentence.

Brookshire and his brother Dustin Gray were driving with Jones in the early morning hours of July 6, 2020, when Brookshire turned around from the front passenger seat and shot Jones, who was in the backseat listening to music with headphones.

The two brothers then stole a shoebox full of cash Jones had been displaying earlier that evening, dumped the murder weapon and Jones’s clothes in Lake Pontchartrain, bought shovels and bleach at a Slidell Lowe’s when it opened at 6 a.m., and buried Jones’s body in a shallow grave in a wooded hunting area in Pearl River County.

Jones’s family reported him missing, setting off an investigation that led police to Gray, who was eventually caught in Colorado and told detectives where the body was buried. Brookshire was arrested July 17, 2020, in Rankin County.

On appeal, Brookshire argued an investigator violated his constitutional rights by questioning him two days after his arrest, after he had already asked for a lawyer and before he had been formally charged or appointed counsel. The appeals court agreed the investigator crossed a constitutional line, noting he referenced Brookshire’s worried parents, told Brookshire that talking was his “only play,” and implied his brother had already told police everything.

But the court upheld the conviction anyway, finding the constitutional violation didn’t affect the outcome given the mountain of other evidence against Brookshire. That included his own confession to his younger brother Andrew, surveillance footage of him buying burial supplies, and the recovery of Jones’s body where Gray said it would be.

Andrew Brookshire testified against his brother as part of a plea deal.

The Supreme Court’s six-justice majority denied review without comment. One justice did not participate.

item.title: Oxford man gets new murder trial after Supreme Court refuses to intervene - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
LAFAYETTE COUNTY — A Lafayette County man convicted of killing his wife will get another shot at trial after the Mississippi Supreme Court on Monday refused to block a lower court’s order throwing out his first-degree murder conviction.

The state’s highest court unanimously declined to reinstate Sherard Eugene Ward’s life sentence, leaving intact a Court of Appeals ruling that said Ward’s jury never got a fair chance to consider a lesser charge.

Ward was convicted in 2023 of murdering his wife, Marisha “Danny” Golden, outside their Oxford-area duplex on September 4, 2020. Multiple neighbors testified they heard a woman scream “No!” before two gunshots. One witness said he saw Ward drop a gun and flee the scene.

Golden was found bleeding in the parking area outside their home. Ward later told his father he shot her.

An autopsy found Golden had been shot twice in the head and neck and also suffered blunt force injuries. All the blood found at the scene was hers.

The Court of Appeals threw out the murder conviction in November, ruling the trial judge wrongly refused to instruct jurors on heat of passion manslaughter, a lesser charge available when a killing stems from sudden rage rather than cold calculation. The sharply divided appeals court said circumstantial evidence including that Golden’s own gun was used, that her blood was found inside the home before any shots were fired, and that Ward’s firearms had been removed from the residence the day before, was enough to warrant the instruction.

Attorney General Lynn Fitch’s office disagreed, arguing the appeals court substituted speculation for evidence. No witness saw Golden threaten or provoke Ward, prosecutors argued, and Ward never took the stand to offer his own account.

The Supreme Court declined without comment to intervene.

Ward’s voyeurism conviction stemming from an incident involving two college student neighbors days before the murder was upheld and is not affected by the new trial order.

No retrial date has been set.

item.title: Mississippi man convicted in armed Dollar General robbery in Carroll County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
GREENVILLE — A federal jury has convicted a Holmes County man of armed robbery and using a firearm during a violent crime in connection with a 2023 holdup at a Dollar General store in Carroll County, authorities said.

Carleone Pate Jr., 21, of Lexington, was found guilty of Hobbs Act robbery and brandishing a firearm during the crime, U.S. Attorney Scott F. Leary announced.

According to court records, the robbery occurred Jan. 19, 2023, when a masked gunman entered the Dollar General in the Black Hawk community and demanded money from the cash register and safe. Law enforcement officers launched a search following the robbery and established perimeter checkpoints in the area.

Pate was later arrested in the woods of northern Holmes County by an off-duty game warden with assistance from a Mississippi Department of Transportation employee, officials said.

Authorities said investigators were able to identify Pate through evidence gathered during the investigation led by the Carroll County Sheriff’s Office, with assistance from the Mississippi Highway Patrol and other agencies.

At the time of the robbery, Pate had recently been released from prison after serving a sentence for aggravated assault convictions in DeSoto County and was out on bail, officials said. U.S. District Judge Debra M. Brown will sentence Pate at a later date.

The case was prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office as part of a federal initiative targeting violent crime.

item.title: Man sentenced to 60 years after pleading guilty in 2021 Tupelo triple killing - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A man has been sentenced to 60 years in prison after pleading guilty to three manslaughter charges in connection with a 2021 Tupelo shooting that killed three people, according to the First Circuit District Attorney’s Office.

District Attorney Jason D. Herring said Taquon Garth entered the guilty pleas Friday.

The charges stem from a July 24, 2021, shooting that resulted in the deaths of Jessica Pannell, Robben Wilson and Norahs Coleman, according to the district attorney’s office.

After accepting Garth’s pleas, Circuit Court Judge Kelly Mims sentenced him to the maximum sentence of 20 years on each manslaughter charge, authorities said.

The three sentences were ordered to run consecutively, resulting in a total sentence of 60 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections.

The district attorney’s office thanked the Tupelo Police Department and Detective Tyler Cook for their work on the case.

Assistant District Attorney Josh Wise prosecuted the case for the state, according to the release.

item.title: Lexington man convicted in Dollar General robbery in Carroll County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HOLMES COUNTY – A federal jury has convicted a Holmes County man of Hobbs Act robbery and using a firearm during the commission of a violent crime in connection with the armed robbery of a Dollar General in Carroll County, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Mississippi.

U.S. Attorney Scott F. Leary said Carleone Pate Jr., 21, of Lexington was found guilty Tuesday. Authorities said Pate had recently been released from the Mississippi Department of Corrections after serving a three-year sentence for two aggravated assault convictions in DeSoto County and was out on bail at the time of the robbery.

According to court records, the robbery happened the morning of Jan. 19, 2023, in the Black Hawk community of Carroll County. Prosecutors said a masked gunman entered the Dollar General at the intersection of Highways 430 and 17 and demanded money from the cash register and safe.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office said the Carroll County Sheriff’s Office responded quickly and began a search that led to Pate’s arrest. Authorities said officers with the sheriff’s office, Mississippi Highway Patrol and other nearby agencies worked to limit possible escape routes by setting up perimeter checkpoints.

Pate was later arrested in the woods of northern Holmes County by an off-duty game warden assisted by a maintenance technician with the Mississippi Department of Transportation, according to prosecutors.

The jury found Pate guilty on both charges and also found that he brandished a firearm during the robbery, authorities said. He will be sentenced at a later date by Chief U.S. District Judge Debra M. Brown.

Leary praised the work of local and state law enforcement, saying federal involvement came through Operation Take Back America, a Justice Department initiative aimed at fighting violent crime in partnership with state and local agencies.

Carroll County Sheriff Clint Walker said the Black Hawk Dollar General is an important part of the community and thanked the deputies, participating agencies, prosecutors and jurors involved in the case.

JACKSON – The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks wants to inform the public of the reopening of J.P. Coleman State Park in Iuka, Mississippi, effective Thursday, April 30, 2026. Park reservations are now open.

item.title: Friday Weather: Rain, rain, rain, with a promising weekend - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
Friday is shaping up to be a washout across the area, so plan accordingly. Expect cloudy skies and steady periods of rain throughout the day, with a high reaching only 59 degrees and northeast winds at 10 to 15 mph. Total rainfall could approach an inch by the time the day is done, with showers continuing into the overnight hours as temperatures drop to around 51. It’s a good day to keep the umbrella close and the travel plans flexible.

The good news is that the weekend brings a significant turnaround. Saturday sees improving conditions with partly cloudy skies and a high of 72, with rain chances dropping to nearly nothing. Sunday looks even better — mostly sunny and pleasant at 77 degrees with light winds. That stretch of nice weather carries into early next week, with Monday climbing to 80 under partly cloudy skies.

If you’ve been waiting on the weather to cooperate for outdoor plans, the weekend is your window.

item.title: Warren County Sheriff warns public about Apple Pay scam message - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
VICKSBURG — The Warren County Sheriff’s Office is warning residents about a scam message claiming an Apple Pay charge has been placed on hold because of unusual activity.

The sheriff’s office shared an example of the message, which tells recipients that a $143.95 Apple Pay charge at an Apple Store in California was temporarily held and urges them to call a phone number for Apple Support.

Authorities said the message is a scam and asked the public to share the warning with others.

Officials did not provide additional details but advised residents to be cautious of unsolicited messages involving account security or payment alerts.

item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
WALNUT GROVE – The Mississippi Department of Corrections says inmates in the barber program at Walnut Grove Correctional Facility have completed the requirements to become licensed barbers.

According to MDOC, members of the facility’s Barber College met the standards of the Mississippi Board of Cosmetology and Barbering.

Superintendent Mike Dixon and Deputy Warden Stephanie Johnston congratulated the inmates on earning their licenses, the department said.

MDOC said the newly licensed barbers are now available to help train others across the agency who want to achieve the same accomplishment.

item.title: Pedestrian killed in late-night crash on Mississippi 57 in Gautier - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GAUTIER – A pedestrian died Tuesday night after being struck by a vehicle on Mississippi 57 near Robinson Still Road, according to the Gautier Police Department.

Police said officers responded to the crash at about 11 p.m. April 28.

Preliminary information indicates the vehicle was traveling northbound when it hit a person who was in the roadway, according to the department.

Emergency personnel with Acadian Ambulance Service attempted lifesaving measures, but the pedestrian died from injuries suffered in the crash, police said.

Authorities described the victim as a white male believed to be between 50 and 60 years old. The Jackson County Coroner’s Office is working to positively identify the man and notify his next of kin, according to police.

The driver remained at the scene and is cooperating with investigators, police said.

The case remains under active investigation.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Gautier Police Department at 228-497-2486.
